label: Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP)

approval.note: Needs a named doctor's approval before real use (owner decision 17 Oct 2026)

note: DRAFT, not approved for real use. Configurable by the clinical team. Required records derived from NICE CG104 (metastatic malignant disease of unknown primary origin in adults, 2010, last updated 26 April 2023, reviewed 16 July 2025 with no change) and the ESMO 2023 cancer of unknown primary guideline (Kramer et al.), quoted verbatim with the section or page on every record. No Indian source exists: NCG India has no CUP guideline, and neither ICMR, TMC nor the MoHFW STGs cover it (owner, 17 Oct 2026). Where NICE and ESMO differ (mammography, tumour markers) the owner chose NICE (R05-Q07). The checklist grows with the NICE diagnostic phase the doctor records (MUO, provisional CUP, confirmed CUP). Nothing here computes a stage, names a likely primary or suggests treatment. To be confirmed by a named doctor and the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). ESMO page numbers are the PDF page numbers (1 to 19) as the guideline library reads the file; the journal page is given under where.
settings_note: The setting is the NICE CG104 diagnostic phase as the doctor records it (the definitions below are NICE's own words from 'Terms used in this guideline'); the system never decides the phase, never computes a stage and never names a likely primary. Item 4.1 derives the required records per setting from the tiers; the gate's labels 'NCG setting' and 'NCG tier' come from rules.py and apply to every protocol, but for this protocol the tiers rest on NICE and ESMO (see tier_basis on each record). When the primary is found, the existing referral moves the Case File to that site's checklist and this check stays as read-only history (R05-Q08).

settings.label: MUO (malignancy of undefined primary origin), as recorded
settings.definition: Metastatic malignancy identified on the basis of a limited number of tests, without an obvious primary site, before comprehensive investigation.
settings.definition_source: NICE CG104, Terms used in this guideline: malignancy of undefined primary origin (MUO)

settings.label: Provisional CUP (after the initial screen, before specialist review), as recorded
settings.definition: Metastatic epithelial or neuro-endocrine malignancy identified on the basis of histology or cytology, with no primary site detected despite a selected initial screen of investigations, before specialist review and possible further specialised investigations.
settings.definition_source: NICE CG104, Terms used in this guideline: provisional carcinoma of unknown primary origin (provisional CUP)

settings.label: Confirmed CUP (after specialist review and special investigations), as recorded
settings.definition: Metastatic epithelial or neuro-endocrine malignancy identified on the basis of final histology, with no primary site detected despite a selected initial screen of investigations, specialist review, and further specialised investigations as appropriate.
settings.definition_source: NICE CG104, Terms used in this guideline: confirmed carcinoma of unknown primary origin (confirmed CUP)

applies_if_note: applies_if on a record is the doctor question that settles whether a conditional record applies (owner decision R07-Q10, 17 Oct 2026: the doctor answers yes or no, audited; sex comes from the registration). It is a specification only: rules.py (V2) reads applies_if_doc_type_present and nothing else, so today every record that carries applies_if is tier c with a condition (shown with the source's own tier and the condition, never counted), as the conditional records of the lung, oral cavity and cervix protocols are. Fields: question (asked of the treating doctor), sex (female, male or null: a registration sex that does not match makes the record not applicable without asking), yes (the tier when the answer is yes), no (the tier when the answer is no, 'none' = not applicable with the reason recorded, R07-Q06), unsettled (the tier while unanswered), source (the guideline line behind the question).

core_data_source: NHS England, Streamlining MDT meetings (2020), p.11 'minimum core data requirements'; aligned with the NCG Virtual Tumour Board case template (India); the clinical trial item also rests on NICE CG104 1.5.1.2 ('Offer patients with confirmed CUP the opportunity to enter clinical trials.') and ESMO 2023 ('inclusion in clinical trials is encouraged [V, A].', PDF p. 14)
policy_basis: PM-JAY Health Benefit Package 2.2 user guidelines (NHA, 2021), section 3.9: pre-authorization is mandatory at each step of cancer care and the decision on appropriate care is to be taken by a multidisciplinary tumour board; NHS England MDT streamlining guidance (2020) pre-listing conditions. Guideline basis of this checklist: NCG India has no guideline for cancer of unknown primary (owner, 17 Oct 2026; none in the NCG library on disk), and neither ICMR, TMC nor the MoHFW STGs cover it, so the records rest on NICE CG104 (UK, 2010, last updated 26 April 2023, reviewed 16 July 2025) and the ESMO 2023 CUP guideline (Kramer et al.), quoted verbatim; an Indian source replaces them as soon as one exists.
